As a Falcone maintainer, I want a pinned inventory of storage consumers and behaviors, so that the replacement preserves existing applications.

## Description

A pinned inventory of storage consumers and behaviors.

Phase: P0 · Effort: M

- [ ] Cover console, SDK, workflow activities, runtime artifacts, presign, multipart, quotas and recursive product bucket deletion.
- [ ] Resolve per-workspace versus per-bucket identity and tenant-versus-workspace quota documentation discrepancies using source fixtures and deployed evidence.
- [ ] Record exact SeaweedFS/SDK versions, public/internal endpoints and any direct S3 users; identify unimplemented backup and capability-builder stubs.

<!-- falcone-s3:S3-CON-002 -->

Parent: [S3-CON](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-s3/issues/1)

## User story

As a platform architect, I want one authority for each bucket, object, policy and key, so that native and external modes integrate with Falcone.

## Description

One authority for each bucket, object, policy and key.

Phase: P0 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-S3-CON-002-1**: Each logical bucket must bind to one explicit native or external provider with trusted tenant/workspace ownership and a versioned writer epoch.
- **FR-S3-CON-002-2**: The service must retain IAM policy, secrets custody, workflow execution and quota definitions under their existing Falcone owners.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publish binding and ownership schemas including managed/adopted modes and capabilities; changing a default affects new buckets only.
- [ ] Use accepted falcone-secrets ADR 0002; do not create a second IdP, secret manager or quota-policy database.
- [ ] Map provider changes to the migration protocol; no automatic fallback to an unrelated backend or shared-prefix allocation default.

## Dependencies

[S3-CON-001](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-s3/issues/16)

<!-- falcone-s3:S3-PROV-002 -->

Parent: [S3-PROV](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-s3/issues/2)

## User story

As an application owner, I want Amazon S3 as a Falcone storage backend, so that I can use managed object storage without changing Falcone APIs.

## Description

Amazon S3 as a Falcone storage backend.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-S3-PROV-002-1**: The Amazon adapter must support qualified bucket/object, conditional, list, multipart and presign operations for general-purpose buckets through maintained SDKs.
- **FR-S3-PROV-002-2**: External object state must remain authoritative at the provider, with uncertain writes recorded and reconciled instead of assuming a local atomic commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test region, virtual-host addressing, temporary credential refresh, SSE profile and scoped permissions in isolated buckets.
- [ ] Cover throttling, lost responses, provider commit followed by local failure and versioned retry duplication; never emulate conditional writes with HEAD then PUT.
- [ ] Publish exact supported SDK/API variants; Express/directory buckets, tables and archival retrieval remain separate profiles.

## Dependencies

[S3-PROV-001](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-s3/issues/19), [S3-AUTH-003](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-s3/issues/27), [S3-KEY-002](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-s3/issues/47)

Parent: [S3-API](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-s3/issues/3)

## User story

As an S3 client developer, I want a defined S3 protocol endpoint, so that standard tools can access authorized Falcone storage.

A defined S3 protocol endpoint.

Parent: [S3-AUTH](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-s3/issues/4)

As a workspace owner, I want storage enforcement of Falcone identities and grants, so that data cannot cross tenant boundaries.

## Description

Storage enforcement of Falcone identities and grants.

- **FR-S3-AUTH-002-1**: The service must issue CSPRNG-generated access keys with scoped actions, resources, expiry and audited rotation/revocation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test cold restoration after metadata/media loss, including independent secrets bootstrap and historical encrypted versions.
- [ ] Distinguish replica safety from backup and disaster RPO; account for full dataset transfer bandwidth rather than promising universal one-hour recovery.

Parent: [S3-MIG](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-s3/issues/14)

## User story

As a rollout owner, I want one writer and an auditable handoff, so that migration cannot lose post-cutover writes.

## Description

One writer and an auditable handoff.

Phase: P3 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-S3-MIG-002-1**: Cutover must quiesce/fence writers, verify final differences and atomically update the authoritative binding epoch and routing.
- **FR-S3-MIG-002-2**: Rollback must reconcile post-cutover writes, versions, deletions, retention and reference mappings before returning authority to the old provider.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Drain/expire presigned writes and multipart sessions; independently controlled external writers require provider-side fencing or verified quiescence.
- [ ] Canary every enabled consumer, credentials, events, quotas and restore path; apply only gates relevant to the selected profile.
- [ ] No blind dual-write, automatic failover to stale data or simple old-snapshot rollback; expose blocked and uncertain operations.

## User story

As an independent reviewer, I want adversarial and fault-injection evidence, so that production data moves only after the chosen profile proves its guarantees.

## Description

Adversarial and fault-injection evidence.

Phase: P2 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-S3-DEV-003-1**: Production candidates must pass profile-specific protocol, cross-tenant, credential, retention, failure and recovery qualification with reviewable evidence.
- **FR-S3-DEV-003-2**: Native qualification must verify acknowledged-write recovery and per-key consistency under crashes, partitions, corruption and stale-worker races.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use operation histories and recovery checksums, not only implementation-shaped unit tests; exercise lost responses and concurrent conditions.
- [ ] Review IAM bypass, forged signatures, SSRF, data leaks and retained-version deletion paths independently.
- [ ] Separate external-only release evidence from native HA evidence; record residual risks and no inherited upstream certification.
